name: Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene

pubchem.title: Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene
pubchem.description: Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene is a bicyclic sesquiterpene that is 1-methylidenedecahydronaphthalene carrying additional methyl and isopropylidene substituents at positions 4a and 7 respectively. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a sesquiterpene, a polycyclic olefin and a carbobicyclic compound. It derives from a hydride of a eudesmane.

evidence: Measured in 6 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.31–9.08% of total volatiles (0.062–1.82mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene is a bicyclic sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule naturally produced by plants. As a volatile compound, it contributes to the complex scent and flavor profiles of the botanical oils it inhabits. A person is most likely to encounter it in the background notes of certain craft beers or tropical fruits.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in the essential oils of hops (Humulus lupulus) and the tropical Surinam cherry (Eugenia uniflora), as well as in certain evergreen trees like the New Zealand black pine (Podocarpus spicatus).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: As a bicyclic sesquiterpene, selina-4(15),7(11)-diene belongs to a family of aromatic molecules known for their diverse biological roles in nature. Currently, researchers are primarily interested in this compound as a botanical marker to understand the chemical profiles of the specific plants that produce it. There is currently no formal pharmacological research on this specific molecule (Oxford level: none found), leaving its potential biological activities an open frontier for future discovery.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: There is currently no formal research literature (Oxford level: none found) evaluating the biological or health effects of this specific molecule.
